newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares slip further, Wall St, dollar weigh.
newsitem.headline: German shares slip further, Wall St, dollar weigh.

text.p: German shares lost ground on Wednesday to close half a percent down after Wall Street and the dollar both slipped. But traders said they see the DAX index holding above the critical 2,700 point level this week.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings in the DAX index of 30 blue-chip shares, made small gains after U.S. September consumer price data came in on target.
But the index then slipped back 13.67 points, or 0.5 percent, to end at 2,705.06., after the Dow Jones fell below the crucial 6,000 point level.
Dealers said a weaker dollar, which came back below 1.54, was also weighing on the market.
Earlier the DAX index ended floor trade down 13.55 points, or 0.5 percent, to 2,714.90, retreating from the record high of 2,728.64 reached briefly on Tuesday.
"We could be ready for a bit of a pause at the moment. But even if it goes down one percent, it's not really serious," one trader said.
The German market has been making record highs for several weeks and each time a new peak is reached, dealers expect the market to consolidate and catch its breath.

The carmaker sector moved against the generally weaker trend, with Volkswagen ending IBIS trade up 4.60 marks at 586.75 marks. BMW ended up 5.10 marks at 901.50 and Daimler Benz rose 56 pfennigs to 87.13.
Dealers said the sector benefitted from positive sentiment after U.S.-based General Motors' rise in third-quarter profits announced on Tuesday.
Utility company Viag was one of the day's main losers, falling almost three percent, to end computer trade down 15.50 marks at 558.50 marks.
Dealers said clouds continued to hang over the company after other German utilty firm RWE dropped out of its joint alliance with British Telecom last week.
